oneLine: Scores every finished warehouse task against the engineered time allowed for it, and reports how each associate and task type is performing.

rows.title: Set the time allowed for a task type
rows.story: An industrial engineer sets how many seconds a task type (pick, pack, slam) should take. A task type with no open standard gets its first one.

rows.title: Set a time for a handling unit, with a team lift
rows.story: The engineer can set a separate time for handling each, case or pallet units. A case standard may also say that a heavy case is a team lift with its own time.

rows.title: Tighten or loosen a standard
rows.story: When a standard is already open, the new one closes it at the same instant. History is never overwritten, so old tasks keep the yardstick they were scored with.
rows.policy: Whenever a standard is already open for the task type and unit, close it as the new one starts

rows.title: Score a finished task
rows.story: When fulfillment-execution reports a task as completed, it is scored against the standard that was in force at that moment, and the associate's idle time since the previous task is worked out.
rows.policy: Whenever a task completes, record its performance exactly once

then.does: keeps a running average task time and idle share per task type, for planning

rows.title: Keep the performance report up to date
rows.story: Each score and each standard change is counted into an hourly report per task type, which supervisors read together with a freshness check. The report has no command of its own.
rows.policy: Whenever a performance or standard event is published, count it once into its task type and hour

hotspots.text: The default idle-gap cap of one hour is a judgment call, not a measured shift length. Operators with other shifts must override it.
fulfillment-execution does not yet send the handling unit or case weight, so unit standards and team lifts never apply to live tasks.
Task types this context does not model (for example REBIN) arrive unclassified: they are counted but never scored.
No access control inside the service: the standards and scorecard routes are open to anyone who can reach it.

opportunities.text: fulfillment-execution could add the handling unit and case weight to TaskCompleted, which would switch the unit standards on.
Standard changes could be published for other contexts to read; today only the scoring facts are shared.
